sources.entry: A framework for pragmatic performance engineering

summary.name: What I've learned about performance engineering
summary.one_liner: A blog post by an engineer at Mailchimp describing a pragmatic framework for finding, investigating, and prioritizing backend performance issues in a large monolithic web application.
use_cases: Deciding where to start a new performance engineering team
Turning vague slowness reports into actionable tickets
Validating a performance hypothesis before optimizing
Building a performance culture across engineering teams
summary.what_it_does: The post lays out a step-by-step framework for performance work: first ensure observability and production profiling exist, then collect qualitative and quantitative data on each issue and write it up as a customer-impact story in a ticketing system. Next it timeboxes investigation (about an hour or two per issue) to find what makes something slow, then treats the finding as a hypothesis to confirm with added instrumentation before fixing. Issues are then prioritized using the gathered context. It also covers organizational practices such as making performance everyone's responsibility, writing clear stories to cross team boundaries, and running office hours for triage.
notable: Emphasizes writing each performance issue up as a customer-impact narrative before fixing it
Treats single observations as hypotheses to disprove with new instrumentation
Recommends office hours to triage one-off performance reports
caveats: Describes the author's experience at Mailchimp; specifics may not transfer to other environments
Focused on backend performance of a monolith; frontend performance is not covered
